correctness.rationale: In Z[[q]] all Euler products used as denominators are units. Set Q=E(q)^p/E(q^p)=1+pR via Frobenius. The quotient F/C telescopes to factors Q(q^{p^j})^{p^{2a−1−j}}, 0≤j<a. For (1+pR)^{p^k}, the term of order h has valuation at least k+h−ν_p(h); modulo p^{k+2} the only terms surviving beyond the constant are linear for odd p, and linear and quadratic for p=2. The latter quadratic has coefficient 2^{k+1}(2^k−1), which contributes with coefficient +1 after normalization mod 2. Thus only j=a−1 can contribute to (F/C−1)/p^{a+1} mod p. For odd p the local quotient (1−z)^p/(1−z^p) contributes −Σ_{h=1}^{p−1}z^h/[h(1−z^p)] after subtracting 1 and dividing by p. Summing over Euler factors produces the stated inverse-divisor sum. At p=2 the local quotient is 1−2z/(1+z), so R counts divisors mod 2 and is supported on squares. The quadratic contributes the Frobenius square, supported on twice-squares. The first term of either correction is −q after reduction; substitution and multiplication by the constant-one C give the claimed first nonzero residue at p^{a−1}, including a=1. Independent direct truncated binomial products verified all 728 inspected coefficients on eight pairs including p=2,a=6, both residue laws and each onset.
residual_risks: Finite checks corroborate normalization and degree placement, not uniform quantification. The formal proof supplies uniformity; non-prime-power t is outside the claim.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Write the prior last factor as (1+pR)^{p^a}; retaining the only surviving binomial terms gives R for odd p and R+R² for p=2. For the same prior Euler quotient, expanding a single factor by binomial coefficients gives −1/h at nonzero residues h mod odd p; collecting divisors is direct coefficient extraction. At 2 the factor simplifies to 1−2z/(1+z), so divisor pairing gives squares and Frobenius gives twice-squares. There is no new obstruction or estimate beyond evaluation of the explicit last factor, and no claim here that the two closed expressions appeared verbatim in the source.
